Plan
1. Append a new subsection for `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-06-10.md` and mark it explicitly as provisional.
   - Keep older report history untouched.
   - Do not add the source doc to the processed-source-doc list.
   - Do not edit or delete `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-06-10.md`.

2. Build the provisional ledger from all concrete recommendations in the 2026-06-10 source doc.
   Count as “concrete recommendations”:
   - the numbered Speed / Cost / Reliability / GH API items,
   - the AI-memory recommendation,
   - the Prompt Cache “Concrete improvements” bullets,
   - the Orchestrator “Smallest safe mitigations” bullets,
   - the Pipeline “Fix:” bullets,
   - every Deep Audit ID (`BUG-*`, `API-*`, `BATCH-*`, `DUP-*`, `CONSIST-*`, `DEAD-*`),
   - every consolidation/dead-call ID (`MERGE-*`, `REUSE-*`, `DEAD-API-*`).
   Do not separately classify pure evidence/metrics tables.

3. Normalize repeated recommendations into stable labels inside the new subsection.
   Expected clusters include:
   - adaptive review pass 2
   - shorter check-run waits
   - CI lint splitting/sharding
   - workspace/context reuse
   - event fan-out reduction
   - AI-memory claim hardening
   - provider retry reclassification
   - Telegram helper hardening / cleanup pagination
   - review/orchestrate batching/reuse
   - shared retry-wrapper consolidation
   - dead helpers (`list_run_log_excerpts`, `read_standalone_state_json`, `autofix_retrigger_has_inflight_peer`)
   Each cluster should name all matching source sections/IDs so no recommendation is lost.

4. Classify each cluster using the required four buckets:
   - `VALID&SAFE`: still true on HEAD, low-blast-radius, no explicit defer/risk tag.
   - `VALID-BUT-RISKY`: still true, but carries explicit `Implementation risk`, `NEEDS_VERIFICATION`, `RISKY_SKIP`, manual-only language, or touches hot review/orchestrator/shared-helper behavior.
   - `STALE-or-already-done`: already landed or made moot by current HEAD.
   - `INVALID`: current HEAD disproves the premise.
   Per issue rules, start from “deferred / risky” for any recommendation with explicit risk/verification/manual-only tagging unless HEAD clearly shows it is already satisfied/stale.

5. Seed the rationale with the current HEAD findings already visible in repo code.
   Important current-state anchors:
   - `scripts/ai_memory.py` already defaults AI-memory push retries to `8`, so the “raise 5→8” piece is stale/already done.
   - `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh` already prefers `ISSUE_META_FILE`, but its cache-miss fallback still does separate issue GETs for labels/body.
   - `scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py::list_run_log_excerpts()` is still definition-only in production code; tests still monkeypatch it.
   - `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml` still defaults `ENABLE_REVIEWER_TWO_PASS=true`, `CHECK_RUNS_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECS=300`, and `WORKSPACE_REUSE_ENABLED=false`.
   - `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh::reviewer_classify_retryable_failure()` still classifies from stderr text and can plausibly misclassify provider `invalid-argument` failures.
   - `scripts/tg_helpers.sh` still uses raw `curl` writes/deletes and deletes while paginating forward.
   - `.github/workflows/orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml` still fetches child/tracking issue data in both the gate and later context step.
   - `scripts/review_collect_pr_metadata.sh` still open-codes PR discussion hydration and still loops fallback `GET /issues/{n}` reads.
   - `.github/workflows/cancel_on_pr_close.yml`, `.github/workflows/mark-stable.yml`, and `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml` still carry inline retry wrappers.
   - `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh::read_standalone_state_json()` and `scripts/gh_helpers.sh::autofix_retrigger_has_inflight_peer()` are still definition-only in this repo.

6. Honor prior deferrals already recorded in the report for overlapping topics unless HEAD clearly changed.
   Especially cross-check against existing report entries for:
   - shorter `CHECK_RUNS_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECS` defaults,
   - partial `implement_diagnose` fallback collapse,
   - `list_run_log_excerpts()` still being present,
   - `read_standalone_state_json()` still being definition-only,
   - broader review/orchestrate batching/reuse items.

Data structures affected
- Markdown-only ledger structure in `analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md`:
  - one provisional subsection for the 2026-06-10 source doc,
  - grouped recommendation labels,
  - one classification per grouped recommendation,
  - concise repo-grounded rationale naming the current file/symbols involved.

API or interface changes
- None to runtime behavior; this is a documentation/report update only.

Potential risks / edge cases
- The 2026-06-10 source doc repeats the same recommendation across multiple sections; omission risk is high unless the provisional section explicitly cross-references duplicates.
- Some recommendations are partially landed, so rationales must say “already partly done, remaining unsafe/deferred piece is X” instead of flattening to fully done/not done.
- Shared-helper surfaces (`scripts/gh_helpers.sh`) may have external consumers not visible from this repo; classify conservatively.
- The issue author explicitly flagged adaptive pass 2, shorter waits, CI splitting, workspace/context reuse, retry reclassification, Telegram hardening, batching/reuse, shared wrapper consolidation, and dead code in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` as likely deferred rather than safe; only override that if current HEAD clearly proves stale/already done.

Testing / verification considerations
- No lint/typecheck/build required if the edit stays markdown-only.
- Verify every concrete 2026-06-10 recommendation is represented once in the provisional section, either directly or via an explicit grouped cross-reference.
- Verify the diff is limited to `analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md`.
- Verify the processed-source-doc list/count and prior history sections remain unchanged.
